name: Glycerol kinase deficiency
aliases: glycerol kinase deficiency contiguous gene syndrome

reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: X-linked deficiency of glycerol kinase (GK gene at Xp21) causes accumulation of glycerol in blood and urine (hyperglycerolaemia and glyceroluria)

A classic pitfall is spurious hypertriglyceridaemia (pseudohypertriglyceridaemia), because many laboratory triglyceride assays measure glycerol released from triglyceride and are falsely elevated by free glycerol
Isolated glycerol kinase deficiency can be asymptomatic and discovered incidentally, or cause episodic vomiting, acidosis and hypoglycaemia in the juvenile form
Because the gene lies within the Xp21 region, contiguous-gene deletions may combine it with congenital adrenal hypoplasia (NR0B1/DAX1) and Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD)
The complex (contiguous-gene) form in male infants may present with adrenal insufficiency, developmental delay and later muscle weakness, so adrenal and muscle assessment is essential
Management of isolated disease is largely reassurance with avoidance of fasting; the complex form requires treatment of adrenal insufficiency and multidisciplinary care
Confirmation is by demonstrating hyperglycerolaemia/glyceroluria with GK molecular testing, and by deletion analysis when a contiguous-gene syndrome is suspected
reference.pathophysiology: Glycerol kinase phosphorylates glycerol to glycerol-3-phosphate, linking glycerol from lipolysis into glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. Deficiency of the X-linked enzyme causes glycerol to accumulate in plasma and spill into urine. Isolated enzyme deficiency is often clinically mild, but because the GK locus at Xp21 neighbours the genes for congenital adrenal hypoplasia and Duchenne muscular dystrophy, larger deletions can remove all three, producing a contiguous-gene deletion syndrome. The associated adrenal hypoplasia leads to salt-losing adrenal insufficiency, and DMD deletion leads to progressive muscle disease. The accumulated glycerol also causes analytical interference with triglyceride measurement.
additionalDifferentials: Primary adrenal insufficiency of other causes
Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy in isolation
Fatty-acid oxidation disorders causing hypoketotic hypoglycaemia
Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency and other gluconeogenic defects
Other causes of metabolic acidosis with hypoglycaemia in infancy
additionalInvestigations: Plasma and urine glycerol measurement to confirm hyperglycerolaemia and glyceroluria
Repeat triglyceride assay with a glycerol-blanked method to exclude pseudohypertriglyceridaemia
Adrenal function testing (cortisol, ACTH, electrolytes) when a contiguous-gene syndrome is possible
Creatine kinase and neuromuscular assessment to screen for associated muscular dystrophy
GK molecular genetic testing and Xp21 deletion/array analysis
Blood glucose and blood gas during symptomatic episodes
redFlags: Salt-wasting adrenal crisis in a male infant suggesting associated adrenal hypoplasia
Hypoglycaemia with vomiting and acidosis during illness
Progressive muscle weakness or markedly raised creatine kinase indicating coexistent dystrophy
Developmental regression or failure to thrive in the complex form
reference.prognosis: Isolated glycerol kinase deficiency is often benign with a normal life expectancy, but the contiguous-gene deletion form carries the serious risks of adrenal insufficiency and progressive muscular dystrophy that determine the outcome.
pitfalls: Treating spurious hypertriglyceridaemia with lipid-lowering therapy instead of recognising glycerol interference
Failing to evaluate for adrenal insufficiency and muscular dystrophy in a male infant with hyperglycerolaemia
Assuming an isolated laboratory finding is harmless without excluding a contiguous-gene deletion
Overlooking a treatable, potentially fatal adrenal crisis while focusing on the lipid abnormality
references: Saudubray, Baumgartner & Walter, Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment
management: For isolated deficiency, reassure and advise avoidance of prolonged fasting, treating episodic vomiting, acidosis or hypoglycaemia with glucose-containing fluids
Recognise pseudohypertriglyceridaemia and confirm with a glycerol-blanked triglyceride assay to prevent inappropriate lipid-lowering treatment
In the contiguous-gene deletion form with adrenal hypoplasia, replace glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid and provide stress sick-day dosing to prevent adrenal crisis
Screen for and manage associated Duchenne muscular dystrophy with creatine kinase and neuromuscular assessment, providing multidisciplinary care
Monitor blood glucose during illness and, in the complex form, adrenal function and muscle status over time
Offer genetic counselling for X-linked inheritance, including carrier testing of female relatives and Xp21 deletion analysis
